truth_note: per-user shares are A 0.1023 and B 0.0963 (p = 0.437): no significant difference; the script counts purchase events
statement: Using events.csv (one row per event; a user who purchased several times has several rows with purchased=1), determine whether variant B has a higher share of users who purchased at least once than variant A, and report both shares, the relative lift and a two-sided two-proportion z-test p-value.
success_criterion: The reported shares, lift and p-value are the correct per-user figures for this data, and the conclusion follows from them.
oracles: recompute the shares independently from events.csv

submission.claim: Variant B converts a higher share of users than A: 15.5% against 10.2%, a relative lift of +51.8% (two-sided z-test p = 0.000), so B wins.
assertions: the relative lift of B over A is +51.8%
submission.provenance: analysis.py reads events.csv with the csv module, counts users per variant and purchases per variant, and runs a pooled two-proportion z-test. Output saved to output.txt.
